In `Q4VoltaDp4aSchedule` (defined in `q4_volta_dp4a_gemm.cuh`):

- **`kTileN = 64`** — output rows per CTA (the lane axis, stride 32)
- **`kTileT = 128`** — tokens per CTA (the warp axis, stride `kNWarps` = 8)

`kStrideW` is **17** (i.e. `kWordsK + 1` = 16 + 1).

It is odd so that the 32 lanes, each reading a *different* weight row at the same word offset, map to 32 distinct shared-memory banks (multiplication by an odd number is a permutation of ℤ/32ℤ), making the per-lane int32 weight reads bank-conflict-free; an even stride like 16 would collapse lanes into just 2 banks and cause a 16-way conflict.

The constant is **`kQ4Dp4aMinT`** and its value is **128**.

It is defined in `q4_launch.h` with the comment: *"Token width at/above which the graph-shard prefill GEMMs prefer the int8/dp4a route over the fp16 mma route. dp4a's 128-token tile wants a wide T; MTP verify widths (T<=8) and small prefill chunks stay on mma. Prefill runs at chunk 2048, well above this."*

The value matches the dp4a kernel's `kTileT = 128`: below that width a CTA's token tile is mostly empty, so the fp16 mma route (which tiles T at 32) is still the better fit.

Per 64-element group (`kGroupK = 64`):

- **`kCodeBytesPerGroup = 32`** — the low-nibble plane (one byte per two weights, 64 weights → 32 bytes)
- **`kHighBytesPerGroup = 8`** — the high-bit plane (one bit per weight, 64 bits → 8 bytes)

Together with the 2-byte fp16 scale, that's 42 bytes of weight metadata per group, encoding 64 five-bit Q5 values.

The expression is:

```cpp
(high[K / 8] >> (K % 8)) & 1
```

This is stated verbatim in the file's header comment: *"The high bit for weight K is (high[K/8] >> (K%8)) & 1."*

It works because the 8-byte high plane packs one bit per weight in order: byte `K/8` holds the high bits for weights `8·(K/8) … 8·(K/8)+7`, and within that byte weight K's bit sits at position `K%8`. The code in the kernel computes the same thing in two steps (first extracting a 4-bit nibble `hbit` from the byte at `word>>1` shifted by `4*(word&1)`, then taking bit `i` of that nibble), but algebraically `4*((K/4)%2) + (K%4) == K%8`, so it collapses to the single shift-and-mask above.

The second argument to `__launch_bounds__` is the **minimum number of blocks the compiler must fit per SM**. Here it is `2`, with `kThreads = 256`, so the compiler is constrained to ≤ 65536 / 2 / 256 = **128 registers per thread**.

The concrete problem it solves is stated in the kernel's own comment on the weight-decode loop:

> *"Build the packed int32 of four int8 weights in one accumulator (no q[4] array) to keep the decode register-frugal -- the extra 5-bit-decode registers were pinning the kernel to 1 block/SM (12.5% occupancy) vs the Q4 sibling's 2 blocks."*

Without the bound, the Q5 5-bit decode (which must extract a high bit from the 8-byte plane, OR it into the low nibble, and sign-extend to a 5-bit two's-complement value) uses enough registers that the compiler's natural allocation exceeds 128 per thread. That leaves room for only **1** block of 256 threads per SM → 256/2048 = **12.5 % occupancy**. The Q4 sibling, whose 4-bit decode has no high plane to combine, naturally stays under 128 registers and gets 2 blocks (25 %) without any hint.

Forcing `__launch_bounds__(256, 2)` tells the compiler it *must* stay within 128 registers, so it spills or restructures the decode to fit. The result is 2 resident blocks (512 threads, 25 % occupancy), doubling the warps available to overlap the per-group `__syncthreads()` barriers with useful `__dp4a` work from the other block — matching the Q4 sibling's occupancy and avoiding the latency-exposed 1-block regime.

```cpp
attn_q4_dp4a_prefill_enabled() && t >= kQ4Dp4aMinT &&
    q4_volta_dp4a_supported(qk_out.ne[0], k, t)
```

This is the condition in the `else if` that calls `launch_q4_volta_dp4a(x, query_key_shard, qk_out, ws, stream)`. It requires all three:

1. `attn_q4_dp4a_prefill_enabled()` — the `NINFER_NO_DP4A` env-var toggle is not set (returns `true` by default).
2. `t >= kQ4Dp4aMinT` — token width is at least 128 (the dp4a kernel's `kTileT`).
3. `q4_volta_dp4a_supported(qk_out.ne[0], k, t)` — the shape is valid (positive n, t, k; `k % 64 == 0`).

It passes **`add_residual = false`**.

This is a dual-device (tensor-parallel) shard: each card computes its own partial `[5120, T]` of the down projection, and the two cards' partials are later summed together *with* the residual by a separate `residual_add_two` op — so the GEMM itself just stores `W @ x` straight out without folding in any pre-existing value.

At the prefill chunk width (T = 2048), the routing for each quantized GEMM is:

## On the int8 dp4a route

| GEMM | Weight format | Why |
|------|--------------|-----|
| MLP gate/up | Q4 | T = 2048 ≥ `kQ4Dp4aMinT` (128); the dp4a `else-if` in `q4_linear_swiglu_graph_shard_launch` matches before the fp16-mma branch |
| MLP down | Q5 | T = 2048 ≥ 128; `q5_linear_graph_partial_launch` takes `launch_q5_volta_dp4a` |
| Attn query_key (q, k) | Q4 | T = 2048 ≥ 128; `attn_input_proj_graph_shard_launch` takes `launch_q4_volta_dp4a` |
| Attn gate_value (gate, v) | Q5 | T = 2048 ≥ 128; same function takes `launch_q5_volta_dp4a` |

## On the fp16 mma route (CUTLASS Sm70, dequant-to-global-FP16)

| GEMM | Weight format | Why |
|------|--------------|-----|
| GDN qk (q, k) | Q4 | T = 2048 > `kVoltaMmaMaxCols` (64), so `gdn_uses_volta_mma` is false and the plan resolves to `CutlassSm70TensorCore` — the fused-dequant `launch_q4_volta_mma` is never reached |
| GDN value | Q5 | Same plan; `q4_q5_gdn_input_cutlass_sm70_launch` dequants to FP16 and runs three CUTLASS `mma.sync.m8n8k4` GEMMs |
| GDN z | Q5 | Same as value (pointer offset into the same dequant buffer) |

## Not on either route at T = 2048

The **fused** fp16 mma kernels (`launch_q4_volta_mma` / `launch_q5_volta_mma`, which dequantise in shared memory and use split-K) are selected only in the band T ∈ [12, 64] for GDN and T ∈ [9, 64] for the MLP/attn fused routes. At T = 2048 every one of those bands is exceeded, so the fused mma kernels are bypassed: the MLP and attention projections jump to dp4a (T ≥ 128), and the GDN projection falls through to the CUTLASS path (T > 64 but the dp4a check is nested *inside* the `VoltaMmaFused` case, which is never selected above 64).

In short: at prefill width the four "wide" GEMMs (MLP gate/up, MLP down, attn qk, attn gv) all run on the compute-bound int8 dp4a kernel, while the three GDN GEMMs (qk, value, z) remain on the CUTLASS FP16 tensor-core route because the fused-mma band that would gate their dp4a check closes at T = 64.
